claim: People differ in how they judge validity: roughly a third use counterexample search, a third a statistical (stated-odds) strategy, the rest are mixed or unclassifiable. Shares vary by sample (statistical 28% to 45%).
agent_test: Not an agent test. Design prior: the scaffold must not assume one reasoner type.

claim: The strategy gap shows only on uncertain inferences (AC, DA, invalid syllogisms, non-sequiturs) and only when asked about logical validity. On MP/MT and on explicit probability ratings the groups answer alike. Qualification: on modus ponens the groups diverge when premise strength is stated (Statistical accept more) or disabling conditions are many (opposite pattern), so the strategies are processing styles, not degrees of logic.
agent_test: Ask the same item as 'is it valid?' and 'how likely?'. Check whether a forced counterexample-search step changes only the validity answers, at equal tokens.

claim: Counterexample reasoners resist belief bias more on conflict items (.76 vs .32 correct); statistical reasoners show a larger belief effect (2.47 vs 1.47 of 4).
agent_test: Run belief-conflict syllogisms with and without a counterexample-search step in S4. Compare conflict accuracy at equal tokens.

claim: Under very short deadlines (3.5 to 5 s) strategy predicts accuracy: counterexample users still reject non-sequiturs (.76 at 3.5 s), statistical users fall to chance (.503). Fast answers are cue-driven, not random: they follow how many alternatives come to mind, and only about 15% of people respond to form alone at 5 s.
agent_test: Hard-cap reasoning tokens. Compare a forced one-line counterexample check against none on non-sequitur and invalid-form items.

claim: Whether working memory or strategy is the main predictor is unsettled. WM matters with unlimited time, strategy keeps predicting under severe limits, and Raven correlates only moderately with strategy (r=.33). Four studies of about 200 each found strategy predicted performance beyond IQ, reflection and numeracy in three of four (not for the conjunction fallacy).
agent_test: Analogue: cross reasoning-token budget with presence of an explicit search step and see which explains accuracy.

claim: Time pressure pushes people toward the statistical pattern, and people switch to the counterexample pattern when time is freed. Reasoners who start with free time keep the counterexample pattern when pressured. Confidence in the fast strategy is lower for statistical answers and predicts switching. Direction confirmed from the 2013 abstract; sample sizes, time limits and percentages are still unopened (full text paywalled).
agent_test: Use cheap estimate by default; switch to counterexample search only when budget allows or a check fails. Compare with always-search at equal tokens. Use a confidence or agreement signal on the quick answer as the switch trigger (d11).

claim: Strategy can be steered by explicit instruction (885 people over two studies), but how well people follow it is limited by their spontaneous strategy, and the effect carried over to the next task (belief-biased inferences, base rates). Statistical reasoners changed most. Per-study sample sizes, effect sizes and durability are still unknown.
agent_test: Instruct the model to reason by counterexample vs by likelihood on a mixed item set. Measure which instruction gains on which item class.

claim: Doing probability questions first shifts later validity judgments toward statistical (updated acceptance 0.96 vs 0.53); validity-first does not alter later probability ratings.
agent_test: Likelihood questions before validity questions in one context vs separate fresh contexts. Supports fresh context per attempt.

claim: Answer format changes processing: scaled certainty tracks exception frequency, dichotomous answers show a different profile (87.1% vs 38.6% accepted for 0 vs 10% exceptions).
agent_test: Compare model output under rating vs yes/no format; code sets the threshold.

claim: The statistical strategy is modelled by min/attachment heuristics (PHM fit r=.90 over 320 points) and language models show the same form-heuristic signature: they almost never answer 'nothing follows' (accuracy near 0% on those items). Further LLM evidence: on NeuBAROCO atmosphere items (answer is neutral) GPT-3.5 got 39.42% and BERT-type models about 0%; across 29 models only 9 beat a Yes/No competence floor.
agent_test: Add a code-triggered 'nothing follows' candidate and counterexample probe for invalid-looking forms. Compare error on invalid schemas at equal tokens.

claim: LLM chains already list alternative scenarios before a likelihood, but model likelihoods are compressed relative to humans, and chain of thought can hurt on defeasible generics (mean drop 11.14 points).
agent_test: Code checks whether stated alternatives change the answer (answer with and without them).

claim: LLMs are weak at actually finding falsifying cases: under 9% of wrong solutions falsified; counterexample validity decays over iterations (69% to 17-30%); prompting a search strategy barely helps. Code verifiers are cheap and accurate (97.7% on 177 audited decisions), but training a model to always disprove destroyed true-claim recognition (0.27 to 0.00).
agent_test: Execute the counterexample search in code (brute force, mutation), never judge it by the model. Measure falsification rate at equal tokens.

claim: An LLM judge accepts about twice as many counterexamples as humans (60% vs 32%).
agent_test: Compare a code checker against a model judge on counterexample validity.

claim: Strategy generalises beyond deduction (causal strength, belief revision, social bias, base rates, denominator neglect) but effects are small in causal tasks (partial eta2 .004 to .038) and absent for the conjunction fallacy.
agent_test: Low priority; no direct agent test.

claim: With free-text answers, counterexample-based uncertainty is more common than probability-based, which challenges a clean two-type split built on rating scales.
agent_test: Elicit free-text uncertainty justifications from the model and classify them; compare with the scale-based split.

claim: Under speed, invalid AC/DA syllogisms are endorsed about as often as valid ones (66% vs 73%), so counterexample search is not the default in fast mode. Consistent with a 5 s study where only about 15% respond logically on abstract AC items.
agent_test: Measure how often the model's brief mode endorses invalid forms; add the search step only on an S1 flag for invalid-looking forms.

claim: No study has run the Markovits 50/90 diagnostic on LLMs or tested a counterexample-vs-statistical prompt switch. Nearest evidence: models answer from fixed Yes/No priors more than from logical form, and question wording changes answers (29 models, 14,320 prompts); reasoning effort changes belief-conflict accuracy for small models (69 vs 99) but not for strong ones.
agent_test: Run the 13-item diagnostic on the agent under both framings.

claim: The strategies are information-processing styles, not logic levels. Statistical reasoners accept modus ponens more when premise strength is stated, and Counterexample reasoners accept it more when disabling conditions are many.
agent_test: Run MP items with stated high probability and with many disabling conditions. Check that the search step does not wrongly reject the strong-premise MP.

claim: Fast answers under a 3.5 to 5 s deadline are not guesses. They follow semantic availability (many alternatives gives more 'invalid') and carry some validity and probability information. Whether this is a logical intuition (De Neys) or a semantic cue (Markovits) is disputed.
agent_test: In capped mode, count how often the answer tracks alternative count rather than form.

claim: More time is not simply more logic. Extra time raised coherent responding but also alternative-generation responses (syllogisms, N=200), and on conflict base-rate problems it raised weight on the stereotype (N=200).
agent_test: Compare short and long reasoning budgets on conflict items with a code-run check. Look for items that get worse with more tokens.

claim: A feeling-of-rightness or confidence signal on a quick answer predicts whether and in which direction a later answer changes (N=289), and confidence in the fast strategy predicted keeping or switching it in 2013.
agent_test: Use agreement across short samples as the confidence signal. Switch to search when it is low. Compare with always-search at equal tokens.

claim: Code-run symbolic reasoning beats plain chain of thought on four of five formal sets with GPT-4 (average +18.4 points over CoT across models) but loses on a set the model already solves (PrOntoQA 98.79 vs 83.20), and depends on faithful translation. No test of counterexample search on invalid AC/DA at equal tokens exists.
agent_test: Run code counterexample search vs plain CoT at equal tokens on invalid AC/DA, belief-conflict and valid items. Report per class and the false-rejection rate.

claim: Chain of thought or higher reasoning effort is not a uniform fix for belief conflict in LLMs: zero-shot chain of thought showed no systematic gain across 14 models (belief bias +10.81 points), while minimum vs medium effort moved GPT-5-nano from 69.22 to 98.84. All-valid test sets hide accept-everything bias.
agent_test: Cross token budget with item validity and belief congruence. Report accuracy on invalid-believable items separately.

claim: A cheap pre-generation router beat random, self-selected and always-think routing in a ranking task (+6.3% NDCG with 49.5% of tokens), but no router has been tested for estimate-vs-search on deduction items.
agent_test: Rule router on form (AC/DA), alternative count and prior-conflict versus always-search and always-estimate at equal tokens.

claim: No test-retest or long-interval reliability data exist for the strategy diagnostic. Stability is documented only within a session. Treat any type label as a within-run measure.
agent_test: Re-run the diagnostic on the agent at different times and with different content sets and report agreement.

claim: The human evidence for the dual-strategy instrument comes from one research network. No independent-lab replication of the 50/90 diagnostic was found; independent labs test neighbouring questions only.
agent_test: None. Treat reported effect sizes as upper bounds.
